To: Operations and Finance Leadership
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: Today
Subject: Shipping plan to meet all destination needs at the lowest total cost

Situation
Our network includes multiple warehouses and factories supplying a broad set of stores, customers, and regional hubs. Each source has finite inventory and handling capacity; each destination has a firm required quantity. Shipping rates vary by route and carrier, and shipments must move in whole units only—no partial loads.

Problem
We need to determine how much to ship from each source to each destination so that:
- No source ships more than it has available.
- Every destination receives its full required quantity.
- The total freight spend is kept as low as possible across all feasible lanes.
The whole-unit requirement adds complexity, as we cannot split a unit across lanes. This plan must strike the right balance between lower-cost routes and source availability while protecting on-time fulfillment and avoiding stranded inventory or shortfalls.

Approach and Expected Outcome
Using the attached supply levels, destination requirements, and per-route shipping costs, we will evaluate feasible lanes and develop a shipment allocation by origin–destination that:
- Honors source inventory limits and destination needs.
- Uses whole-unit quantities only.
- Achieves the lowest attainable total shipping cost while maintaining service commitments.
The resulting plan will be operationally executable and ready for carrier booking and warehouse wave planning.
